If a beam of hydrogen atoms in their ground state (with n 5 1, , 5 0, m 5 0) is sent through a magnetic field whose intensity increases in the plane perpendicular to the flight of the beam, it splits into two beams, each containing half of the atoms (Fig. 5.15). The pioneering experiment of this type is called the Stern–Gerlach experiment after the German physicists who performed it, Otto Stern and Walther Gerlach.
